staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout.

classification.classification_note: The public issue labels the witness as a heap-buffer-overflow READ, but the saved AddressSanitizer report is `use-after-poison` because the AFL++ driver allocates a larger input buffer and poisons bytes beyond the current input size. At source level the bug is a one-byte read past the logical end of the 2-byte input after trailing whitespace is skipped.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42512152 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42512152
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the two-byte file `5b 20` (`[ `). `magic_buffer()` forwards those bytes to `file_buffer()`, and `file_is_json()` materializes parser cursor `uc` and end pointer `ue` from `b->fbuf` and `b->flen == 2`. Top-level `json_parse()` reads the first byte `'['`, increments `uc` to the second byte, and dispatches into `json_parse_array()`. Inside the array parser, `while (uc < ue)` admits the loop body because one byte remains. `json_skip_space()` then consumes the trailing space and returns `uc == ue`, but the vulnerable code performs no `if (uc == ue) goto out;` check at that point and immediately evaluates `if (*uc == ']')`. That dereferences one byte at `ue`, past the logical 2-byte input, and the saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `use-after-poison READ of size 1` at `/src/file/src/is_json.c:187:7`. The patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting the missing end-of-input guard immediately after `json_skip_space()` in `json_parse_array()`.

source.code:
const unsigned char *uc = CAST(const unsigned char *, b->fbuf);
const unsigned char *ue = uc + b->flen;
source.description: First project parser step that materializes the attacker-controlled bytes and their exact logical extent into the JSON parser state.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly two bytes `5b 20` (`[ `). At this statement `uc` points at byte 0 `'['` and `ue` is computed as one-past-end of that 2-byte logical input.

root_cause.description: After `json_skip_space()` may advance `uc` to `ue`, the array parser dereferences `*uc` without the missing `if (uc == ue) goto out;` guard that the patch inserts at this exact point.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. Evaluating this condition reads one byte from `uc == ue`, so the parser dereferences the third byte of a logical 2-byte input.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled input size is first materialized here as the end pointer `ue`. Later `json_skip_space()` advances `uc` exactly to this boundary, and the missing post-skip guard lets the parser dereference at `ue`.

parser_admitted.description: The first PoC byte is `'['`, so top-level JSON parsing takes the array arm and enters `json_parse_array()`, the branch containing the missing post-whitespace end check.

coarse_trace.summary: After `magic_buffer()` receives the exact 2-byte witness, `file_buffer()` routes it into `file_is_json()` as candidate JSON text.
The JSON classifier materializes `uc` and `ue` from the buffer, then reads the leading `'['` and dispatches into `json_parse_array()` with the cursor on the second byte.
The array loop's pre-skip bound check passes while one byte remains, and `json_skip_space()` consumes that trailing space so the cursor becomes `uc == ue`.
Without the patch's missing `if (uc == ue) goto out;` guard, the parser evaluates `*uc` at line 187 and reproduces the saved 1-byte AddressSanitizer out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.code:
const unsigned char *uc = CAST(const unsigned char *, b->fbuf);
const unsigned char *ue = uc + b->flen;
fine_trace.note: Source. `file_is_json()` turns the attacker-controlled buffer pointer and length into parser cursor `uc` and fixed end pointer `ue`. For the exact witness `5b 20`, `uc` starts on `'['` and `ue` is the boundary immediately after the second byte.
Top-level JSON parsing reads byte 0 as `'['`, advances `uc` to byte 1, and selects the array parser. That control decision is what places the remaining single-byte tail under `json_parse_array()`.
This is the last explicit in-bounds guard before whitespace skipping. It succeeds because after step 2 the cursor is on byte 1 and one byte still remains before `ue`.

With the exact witness, the only remaining byte is ASCII space `0x20`, so `json_skip_space()` consumes it and returns `uc == ue`. The parser cursor has now moved from the second byte to one-past-end of the logical input.

Root cause. After step 4 made `uc == ue`, the array parser still falls through to this dereference site without rechecking end-of-input. `json_parse_object()` has the missing pattern immediately after its own `json_skip_space()` call (`if (uc == ue) goto out;`), and the patch adds that same obligation here.

Sink. Evaluating the condition reads one byte from `uc == ue`, i.e. the third byte of a logical 2-byte input. The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison READ of size 1` at `/src/file/src/is_json.c:187:7`; the address is inside the AFL++ driver allocation but exactly one byte past the current input size because the unused tail is user-poisoned.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the faulting address 2 bytes inside a 1048576-byte driver allocation. The AFL++ driver poisons bytes beyond the current input size, so the source-level one-byte read past the 2-byte logical input surfaces as `use-after-poison`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch inserts `if (uc == ue) goto out;` immediately after `uc = json_skip_space(uc, ue);` in `json_parse_array()`. That is the exact missing guard on the witnessed path. Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from saved Stage 01 sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, the staged vulnerable source checkout, and the exact PoC bytes

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan top frame is `json_parse_array /src/file/src/is_json.c:187:7`, which is the exact sink recorded here.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `json_parse_array -> json_parse -> file_is_json -> file_buffer -> magic_buffer -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; the fine trace makes explicit the cursor and end-pointer transitions inside those same project frames.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact two-byte witness sets `ue` from `b->flen == 2`, `json_parse()` advances `uc` past `'['`, `json_skip_space()` advances `uc` to `ue`, and the next line dereferences that `uc` as `*uc`.

format.name: 2-byte JSON array prefix
format.contract: Use the exact 2-byte file `5b 20` (`[ `) and no other bytes. This GT is grounded only for that singular witness: byte 0 must be `'['` so `json_parse()` selects `json_parse_array()`, byte 1 must be JSON whitespace so `json_skip_space()` advances the array cursor to `ue`, and the input must end there with no closing `]`. Stage 02 does not generalize beyond this exact two-byte sample.
